prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map establishes a top-down layered layout where the camera wearer at the bottom faces a seated person across a horizontal tray (~0.5 m away), whose torso is at the top (~0.6–0.8 m away, head cropped out of view) and whose feet rest in a basin below the tray (~0.9–1.0 m away) next to the tiled floor (~1.1–1.3 m away). Both the camera wearer's hands and the seated person's hands—one centred on the tray and one on the right edge (~0.5–0.7 m away)—are within arm's reach of the tray, while a tall blue basket and pink bowl sit on the left side of the tray within reach. Across frames 1 to 4, the camera wearer's left forearm rises closer to the camera (brightening to ~0.25–0.35 m) and arches over the seated person's right hand while the right hand shifts rightward (~0.25 m apart in frame 4) before retreating slightly in frame 5, partially occluding the tray and the other person's hand beneath. Compared to the RGB strip, the depth map makes it much easier to see the vertical height of the blue supply basket and the elevation of the camera wearer's arched left forearm above the flat tray and recessed floor below. However, it is unreliable for thin objects resting flat on the surface—the metal tool, nail file, and green nippers merge into the tray's depth plane—and it blurs the exact boundary where the two people's hands touch.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map outlines the spatial occupancy of the two people within ~0.3–0.8 m of the camera: the seated person at the top facing toward the camera wearer with both arms extended forward onto the tray, and the camera wearer's arms and black-clad legs extending from the bottom into the lower foreground. Across the five frames, the masks show the camera wearer's left arm sweeping upward and leftward in frames 2–4 to overlap and occlude the seated person's right forearm on the centre of the tray, while the camera wearer's right arm moves rightward in frame 4 and holds a tool on the right in frame 5. Unlike the RGB image, the segmentation map explicitly attempts to partition foreground human limbs from the surrounding floor and work surface, and in frame 5 it cleanly separates the seated person's right arm (pink mask) from the camera wearer's two arms and legs (green mask) where they meet at ~0.5 m depth. However, the map is largely unreliable: it completely omits the tray, manicure tools, and supply basket, mislabels the pink bowl on the left as a 'sports ball' in frame 1 and a basket item as a 'carrot' in frame 5, and severely fragments and swaps 'person' instance IDs between the two people's limbs and the tray surface in frames 2–4.
descriptions.pose: The pose map isolates the positions and finger orientations of hands (magenta skeletons) within arm's reach (~0.35–0.65 m in front of the camera wearer) over the tray, while both people's torsos and out-of-view heads produce no yellow body skeletons. In frame 1, two hand skeletons appear close together near the centre (~0.05–0.1 m apart); in frame 2, only the right-side hand skeleton is present; and in frames 3–5, the left and right hand skeletons separate horizontally from ~0.1 m to ~0.25 m apart as the camera wearer's right hand moves rightward to set down the file and pick up the nippers. In frame 5, a third hand skeleton is also detected at the upper right (~0.65 m away), corresponding to the seated person's left hand resting on the right edge of the tray. This map reveals fine 3D finger articulation and curl—such as the pincer posture of the camera wearer's hands and the splayed fingers of the left hand in frame 5—that are harder to parse against the cluttered background in RGB. However, it is unreliable because it fails to detect any body pose for either person, drops the camera wearer's raised left hand in frame 2, and fails to distinguish both overlapping hands where the camera wearer's left hand occludes the seated person's right hand in the centre.
